front.title: Operational Telemetry Comparability for IP Performance Measurements

abstract.t:
Operational telemetry is often used to compare network performance across observation points, traffic classes, service instances, paths, devices, and time intervals. The numeric value of a metric is not sufficient for such comparison unless the observation context and the comparability conditions are also known.
This document describes a common interoperability problem in operational measurement systems: values such as delay, loss, ECN marking, queue occupancy, packet counts, byte counts, and flow correlation identifiers can be exported from different observation points or under different aggregation rules while still appearing to be directly comparable. A collector or controller can therefore combine values that do not describe the same measurement domain.
The document defines requirements for describing the observation point, metric source, aggregation interval, traffic class, flow scope, sampling rule, timestamp basis, freshness, and comparability domain associated with operational telemetry used for IP performance measurement. The goal is to make operational measurement results easier to compare without prescribing one measurement protocol, one data model, or one congestion control mechanism.
